newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca to boost U.S. salesforce by 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca to boost U.S. salesforce by 20 pct.

text.p: Britain's Zeneca Group Plc said on Tuesday it planned to expand its U.S. salesforce by more than 20 percent to deal with a rush of new products, including the potential launch later this year of migraine drug Zomig and schizophrenia treatment Seroquel.
In a statement Zeneca said it was adding 250 sales representatives on a temporary contract basis to its existing permanent sales force of 1200.

Sales of Zeneca's products in the U.S. rose 20 percent in the first half of 1996 to $732 million, and the company launched seven new products there during the year, including its new asthma drug Accolate.
The latest expansion follows a major increase in permanent representatives in early 1996.

In an interview with Reuters, chief executive David Barnes said the new representatives, who are being recruited and managed by HealthCare Promotions of New Jersey, would not be involved with Zeneca's key cancer portfolio.

Barnes said they would be used to promote Zeneca's cardiovascular range, including hypertension drug Zestril and newly-launched calcium channel blocker Sular, Accolate and "in due course Seroquel and Zomig."
Zeneca has high hopes for Seroquel and for Zomig, which it obtained from Glaxo Wellcome Plc last year as a condition of the latter group's merger.

"The 1996 recruitment dealt with expanding the permanent sales force, but as we still have two more major products to launch in the U.S, hopefully in 1997, this will help us to deal with the current bulge and the additive bulge," Barnes said.
The chief executive added that some of the temporary staff might be converted to full-time positions in the future.
